'''Therese Charlotte Biedl''' is an Austrian [[computer scientist]] known for her research in [[computational geometry]] and [[graph drawing]]. Currently she is a professor at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Canada.<ref name="profile">[https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/people-profiles/therese-biedl Faculty profile], Univ. of Waterloo, retrieved 2017-12-08.</ref>

== Education ==
Biedl received her Diploma in Mathematics at [[Technische Universität Berlin]], graduating in 1996
and earned a Ph.D. from [[Rutgers University]] in 1997 under the supervision of Endre Boros.<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Therese Biedl|id=96437}}</ref><ref name="cv">[https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~biedl/research/cv.pdf Curriculum Vitae], Univ. of Waterloo, retrieved 2017-12-08.</ref>

== Research ==

Biedl's research is in developing algorithms related to graphs and geometry. [[Planar graphs]] are graphs that can be drawn without crossings. Biedl develops algorithms that minimize or approximate the [[Area (graph drawing)|area]] and the height of such drawings.{{ran|A}} With Alam, Felsner, Gerasch, Kaufmann, and Kobourov, Biedl found provably optimal [[Time complexity#Linear time|linear time algorithms]] for proportional contact representation of a maximal planar graph.{{ran|C}}

== Awards ==
Biedl was named a Ross & Muriel Cheriton Faculty Fellow in 2011, a recognition of the reach and importance of her scholarly works.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross & Muriel Cheriton Faculty Fellowship {{!}} Cheriton School of Computer Science|url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/about/faculty-fellowships-and-awards/ross-muriel-cheriton-faculty-fellowship|website=Cheriton School of Computer Science|access-date=9 December 2017|language=en|date=10 February 2017}}</ref>
